opennyai_summary.4_March_2025__facts:
The petitioner challenges the impugned order passed by the third respondent in Na.Ka.No.E-2266729-2024-J4, dated 30.11.2024 with a consequential direction to the respondents 1 to 4 to award the petitioners adequate, fair and reasonable compensation for the houses constructed by them and also direct the respondents to allot appropriate alternate lands by granting assignment pattas in the name of the petitioners. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
protecting the possession of the petitioners, the State had moved a vacate injunction application and after obtaining orders from this Court, all the petitioners were forcibly dispossessed and the houses https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 10/03/2025 05:38:20 pm ) constructed by the petitioners were also raised to the ground.
7.From the impugned order, I am able to see that the third respondent has rejected the request for payment of compensation on the ground that under Section 77 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Act, 2013, the compensation can be paid only to the title owner, who admittedly, is the fifth respondent herein and therefore, the request of the petitioners in that regard has been rejected.
opennyai_summary.4_March_2025__ANALYSIS:
However, in so far as the individual representations made by the petitioners for alternate accommodation, I find that there is no opportunity given to the petitioners to put forth their claims and there has been no consideration of such requests in and by the impugned order.
9.Admittedly, all the petitioners, even according to the fifth respondent, have put up superstructures out of their own funds.
However, considering the fact that the petitioners all hail from weaker sections of society and being a welfare State, the third respondent ought to have taken a sympathetic view at least with regard to allotment of alternate lands in any of the prevailing schemes, where, the petitioners can be accommodated in order to give them a roof to live under.
opennyai_summary.arguments: No doubt, as contended by the learned Counsel for the fifth respondent, the petitioners have agreed that at the time of determination of the respective tenancies/leases, they would surrender the superstructure in favour of the fifth respondent and would not make any claim.
opennyai_summary.4_March_2025__decision:
sympathetic grounds, I am inclined to set aside the impugned order and remit the matter back to the third respondent.
Accordingly, the impugned order, dated 30.11.2024 is set aside the matter is remanded to the file of the third respondent.
The petitioners shall give fresh applications to the third respondent seeking alternate accommodation in any of the welfare schemes that are in force.
On such applications being made by the individual petitioners, the third respondent shall consider the same on a case to case basis not only on the individual merits of the claims made by the respective petitioners, but also taking a sympathetic view in the matter, considering that the petitioners have put up constructions on the lands belonging to the fifth respondent and they have been forcibly evicted without any compensation for the superstructure put up and also considering the fact that Unknown vs The Secretary To Government on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163240856/
4 the petitioners and their families are on the streets today.
The third respondent is directed to afford an opportunity to all the petitioners individually to present their respective difficulties and hardships and thereafter, the third respondent shall pass orders on merits and in accordance with law.
The entire exercise shall be completed within a period of twelve weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
11.The Writ Petition is disposed of with the above directions.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
The first ground is that the award was passed in the name of a dead person even though the third respondent was informed on more than one occasion that the original owner of the property namely,
Radhabai died on 31.07.2014 and therefore, the award must be held to be null and void.
The Act was once again revived by the Tamil Nadu Amendment Act 38/2019.
Thereby, the benefits of the Central Act 30/2013 has to be considered for determination of compensation on the date of notification under Section 11 of the Act as provided under Section 26 of the Act 30/2013.
Since the same has not been complied with, the award passed by the third respondent has to be held to be null and void.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
5. In the case on hand, the original owner of the property namely, Radhabai was the owner of the property and she died on 31.07.2014.
On that ground alone, the award has to be held to be null and void.
Under Sub-Section 11 of Section 7, determination of compensation must be made within a period of six months from the date of reference to the Collector.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
In spite of the fact that the same was brought to the notice of t h e t h i r d r e s p o n d e n t , t h e t h i r d r e s p o n d e n t p r o c e e d e d t o p a s s t h e a w a r d https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
The award was passed on 05.11.2020 by the third respondent when 1997 Act was in force.
In the case on hand, the award has not been passed within the time prescribed.
That apart, the Act was held to be invalid by the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court on 03.07.2019 and the Act was thereafter revived by the Tamil Nadu Amendment Act 38/2019, which provided for the benefits of the Central Act 30/2013.
This was not even taken into consideration by the third respondent and on this ground also, the award has to be held to be null and void.
In view of the above, the impugned award passed by the third respondent in Award No.1/2020 dated 05.11.2020 is hereby quashed.
There shall be a direction to the third respondent to re-determine the compensation in line with the Central Act 30/2013 by taking the base date as 01.01.2014 and compensation shall be paid to the petitioners within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of the order.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
In the result, this Writ Petition is allowed in the above terms.
There shall be no order as to costs.
